philosophy: Dead strategies are institutional memory. Do not delete them. Six months from now, someone will 'discover' the exact same failed idea. This file prevents that.

MM-002.name: Monday Gap Fade (MGF-01)
MM-002.verdict: The 12-year daily data tells the truth. PF 0.65 portfolio-wide. Bootstrap P(PF<1) = 100%. NOT A SINGLE YEAR has PF > 1.1. The earlier H4 backtest showing PF 1.17 was a short-window artifact (2023-2026 only). Gap fade works ONLY in RANGING/LOW_VOL regimes. Without a regime filter, this is a slow bleed. NOTE: If regime detection is built, this strategy could potentially be revived as a RANGING-only deployment on NZDUSD/USDCHF/EURJPY. But never as an unconditional portfolio strategy.
MM-002.revival_condition: RANGING/LOW_VOL regime filter + NZDUSD/USDCHF only + live paper trading confirmation

MM-003.name: Key Level Defensive Fade (KLF-01)
MM-003.verdict: Weekly key level wick rejections don't produce follow-through. 35% WR suggests 'wick and close back inside' is not reliable rejection — it often represents continuation before a breakout. Only ETHUSD pair was marginally profitable (PF 2.5) but sample too small to trust.

MM-009.name: Liquidity Sweep Quick Reversal (LSQR)
MM-009.verdict: PF 0.84 portfolio-wide despite instrument locking. Was marginally profitable in earlier tests but V4 shows deterioration. ETHUSD pair alone PF 2.0 (67% WR) but tiny sample. The liquidity sweep concept is valid but better executed through the full 8-Gate SMC pipeline (Gate 5). Standalone is too noisy.

MM-019.name: Order Block Retest
MM-019.verdict: SMC refinement layer failed as standalone. OB retest without full 8-Gate pipeline context produces too many false signals. This should ONLY run as Gate 5 filter inside the SMC system, never independently.
MM-019.note: This is NOT a standalone strategy. It is a pipeline filter. Do not resurrect as a signal generator.

MM-020.name: Fair Value Gap Fill
MM-020.verdict: FVG fill without full 8-Gate context is unprofitable. FVGs are too common and need structural confluence to filter. Same as MM-019: Gate 5 filter, not standalone signal generator.
MM-020.note: This is NOT a standalone strategy. It is a pipeline filter. Do not resurrect as a signal generator.

MM-021.name: Market Structure Shift Entry
MM-021.verdict: MSS standalone produces massive drawdown. 26.5% WR indicates shift detection is too sensitive without the full gate pipeline. This is a Gate 6 component, not a standalone strategy.
MM-021.note: This is NOT a standalone strategy. It is a pipeline filter. Do not resurrect as a signal generator.

MM-022.name: Session High/Low Raid + Reversal
MM-022.verdict: Generated ZERO signals. Session raid detection too restrictive. Session extremes already captured by Gate 1 (Session) and Gate 5 (Liquidity Sweep) in 8-Gate SMC. No standalone value.

MM-023.name: London Breakout (LB-01)
MM-023.verdict: Classic London breakout fails: 41% WR on 372 trades. Asian range compression + London breakout is a well-known setup that has been largely arbed away. Compressed ranges break out in random directions.

MM-024.name: NY Reversal (NYR-01)
MM-024.verdict: Catastrophic: 9.7% win rate, -0.81 avg R. London session extreme + candlestick reversal at NY open does not work. London extremes frequently extend into NY; they don't reverse.

MM-025.name: ATR Compression Breakout v2 (ACB-01)
MM-025.verdict: Despite ATR contraction, volume confirmation, and 4-bar hold rule, this is still effectively a Donchian channel system with extra steps. 31% WR on 208 trades confirms: volatility compression breakouts in isolation don't produce directional edge. Markets often compress then range further.

SMC_8G.name: 8-Gate SMC Pipeline
SMC_8G.verdict: Strong edge on 2-3 year H4 data. CRITICAL DATA LIMITATION: H4 data limited to ~2-3 years. Needs 90-day paper trading before any capital deployment.
SMC_8G.risk: H4 data limitation. LTF confirmation only available for ~60 days. Real-time execution may differ.

MM-005.name: RSI Divergence Reversal
MM-005.verdict: PF 2.0 looks great but 6 trades is meaningless. Cannot validate. Do NOT deploy until sample reaches 30+ trades.
MM-005.risk: Tiny sample. Any PF with 6 trades is noise.

MM-012.name: Gap Fill Weekend (GPFL)
MM-012.verdict: Barely profitable. Same alpha source as MM-002 (weekend gap). Correlation with MM-002 is low (0.06) but both trade the same gap. Marginal edge at best.
MM-012.risk: Low correlation with MM-002 is misleading — they trade the same phenomenon.

lessons_learned: Indicator-based strategies (RSI, MACD, Bollinger, Stochastic, Ichimoku) consistently fail across all instruments. The market does not reward simple indicator signals.
SMC (Smart Money Concepts) is the only approach that shows a consistent edge, and only when all 8 gates are combined. Individual SMC components (OB, FVG, MSS) fail as standalones.
Session-based strategies (London Breakout, NY Reversal) are well-known and appear to be arbed away. They fail in modern markets.
Volatility compression breakouts don't work because compression often leads to more compression, not expansion. The market can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent.
Gap fade strategies have a REGIME DEPENDENCY: they work in ranging/low-vol conditions and fail in trending/high-vol. Without a regime filter, they are net losers.
Any strategy showing PF > 2.0 with fewer than 30 trades should be treated as UNVALIDATED noise.
The difference between H4 and daily data can turn a 'profitable' strategy into a loser. Always validate on the longest available data window.
Correlation between strategies trading the same phenomenon (gap fade vs gap fill) may be low month-to-month but they share the same failure mode: trending markets.
